situation: My brother and sister aren't speaking because of a fight over who hosts Christmas with our dad. Both keep calling me to vent. I want to help without being in the middle. My sister just called again.
reply: That sounds really frustrating, and I'm glad you told me. I love you both, so I'm not going to take sides or pass things along to Dan. I think this needs saying to him directly. Want me to set up a call with the three of us on Sunday? I'll tell him exactly the same thing.
note: Offer to host the conversation, never to carry the message.

situation: My friend Leah is mad at me because I won't take her side against Chloe after their falling out over the bridesmaid thing. She says I'm being fake.
reply: I get that you wanted me in your corner, and I'm sorry that's hard. I'm not taking sides between you and Chloe, and that's not me being fake, it's me caring about you both. I'm still your friend, and I'll still see you at dinner on Friday.
note: Repeat the position calmly and reaffirm the friendship; don't relitigate their fight to prove you're neutral.

situation: Team lead here. Two of my engineers, Omar and Beth, have been sniping at each other in code reviews. I've spoken to each privately; now I'm hosting a joint meeting tomorrow. How do I open it?
reply: Thanks for coming, both of you. I'm not here to decide who was right in past reviews. Let's keep this to how code reviews work from here on: one person talks at a time, and we leave with one thing we both agree to try for the next two weeks. Omar, do you want to start with what a good review looks like to you?
note: Neutral on the history, clear on the rules. Send a written summary of the agreement afterwards.

situation: 我跟阿杰、小雨三个人合租。他们俩因为打扫轮值和水电费闹翻了，一周没说话，两个人都跑来跟我吐槽。刚才小雨让我帮她跟阿杰说一声，下个月网费她不跟他平摊了。
reply: 小雨，我知道这事让你挺憋屈的，你愿意跟我说我很理解。不过我不想在你们俩中间传话，传着传着意思就变了，对谁都不好。网费的事还是你直接跟阿杰说比较好。要不这周日晚上八点我们三个在客厅坐下来聊一次？只聊网费和打扫，一个人说完另一个再说，争取先定下一件事。我也会这样跟阿杰说，不是突然袭击。
note: 拒绝当传话筒，但主动搭一个直接对话的台子；两边说一样的话，才是真的中立。

situation: My mom and my aunt haven't spoken since Grandma's funeral in June, over who gets her house. I offered to host a call between them and my aunt texted: 'Never. And if you keep pushing this I'll stop talking to you too.'
reply: I hear you, and I'm not going to push. I love you both and I'm staying out of the house question. The offer stands if you ever want it, and either way I'll see you for Sunday lunch on the 11th like we planned.
note: When one side refuses, drop it cleanly and protect your own relationship with her; the offer stays open without pressure.

situation: I chair our community garden committee. I got two members, Frank and Delia, together to sort out their fight over the shared tool shed, and 10 minutes in they're talking over each other and Frank just said 'this is pointless'. I need to stop it.
reply: Let's stop here for today. I don't think we'll get further right now, and that's okay; it's obvious you both care about this garden. I'd like to try again on Saturday the 10th after the workday, just on the shed schedule. If it helps, I can ask someone from the council's free mediation service to sit in.
note: Pause kindly, name the shared goal, and offer a narrower second try or a neutral professional. Don't rule on the shed in the room.

situation: I manage a small sales team. Priya and Luke have been fighting over who owns the Harmon Foods account since the territory change. In our joint meeting today we agreed Priya owns it from Oct 1, Luke hands over his notes and joins the next two calls, and disputes come to me instead of the team chat. I want it in writing to both.
reply: Thanks both for today. To confirm what we agreed: Priya owns the Harmon Foods account from Thursday 1 October. Luke will share his account notes and contacts by Friday 2 October and join the next two Harmon calls to make the introductions. If anything about the account is unclear from here, bring it to me rather than the team channel. Let's check in together on Tuesday 13 October.
note: The written summary goes to both at once, in the same words: neutral on who was right, clear on who does what next.

situation: 我不是领导，只是组里的普通同事。小王和小李为了一个项目排期闹得很僵，两个人都私下跟我抱怨对方。今天小王又来找我，说：“你评评理，是不是他太过分了？”
reply: 我知道这事让你挺窝火的，你愿意跟我说我明白。不过我跟你俩都是同事，谁对谁错我真不好评，评了反而帮倒忙，你跟我说的我也不会传给小李。排期的事还是你俩直接聊最快，要不约个会议室把时间线摊开对一对？需要的话，我可以帮你想想怎么开口。
note: 同级同事被拉去评理：先接住情绪，说明不站队、不传话，再把他推向直接沟通；领导的角色留给领导。

situation: 大学四个室友的群里，阿敏和小月因为国庆去厦门的AA账吵起来了，越说越难听，其他人都不敢出声。钱是我统一垫付的，民宿和包车的单据都在我这儿。我想在群里说点什么。
reply: 两位，看得出这事让你们俩都挺不舒服的，我不站谁那边。钱是我垫的，今晚我把民宿、包车和吃饭的每一笔单据整理成表格发到群里，大家按实际花费看。对得上的就按表来，有出入的地方你们俩私下直接聊，需要的话周六晚上我们三个语音一下，我在旁边。群里这事就先聊到这儿。
note: 群里公开吵，先把争执挪出群聊；垫钱的人只提供事实，不判谁对谁错，再搭一个直接对话的台子。

situation: My two closest friends, Jess and Mia, haven't spoken since a fight over a flat they were meant to share. My 30th is Saturday Oct 17 at my place and I want both there. I'd like to tell each of them before they see the other on the invite.
reply: Heads up so there are no surprises: I've invited Mia to my 30th on Saturday the 17th as well. I'm not trying to set anything up, and I'm telling her the same about you. I'd really love you there. If it feels like too much, I get it, and we'll do dinner just us the week after.
note: Same words to both, sent separately: no ambush, no engineered reunion, and a real out that protects your friendship with each.

situation: My sons, Ethan (16) and Leo (13), have been at war for weeks over the shared Xbox, slamming doors and texting me separately to complain about each other. I've heard each of them out. Tonight after dinner I'm sitting them down together. How do I open it?
reply: Thanks for sitting down, both of you. I'm not here to decide who's right, and I'm not going to keep passing complaints back and forth. Tonight we're only talking about the Xbox, nothing else. One person talks at a time, no interrupting, and let's try to leave the table with one thing we agree on, even if it's just who has it this Saturday.
note: Even as the parent, stay neutral on who's right: one topic, one speaker at a time, and aim for one small agreement rather than a full peace deal.

situation: I'm a shift supervisor at a restaurant. A server, Jade, told me a line cook, Ryan, keeps commenting on her body and has brushed against her twice. She asked me to 'just sit you both down and sort it out' because she doesn't want it to be a big deal.
reply: Jade, thank you for telling me, and I'm really sorry this has been happening. What you've described isn't a disagreement I can sort out between the two of you; it has to go through the company, and that's what protects you. I'm taking it to our general manager, Lisa, today, and I'll keep it as private as I can. Until it's dealt with, I won't put you and Ryan on the same shifts. Is there anything else you need from me right now?
note: Comments about her body and unwanted touching are not a two-sided dispute: don't hold a joint sit-down; report it through the channel your workplace policy names.

situation: 我妈从老家过来帮我们带刚满半岁的孩子，跟我老婆因为孩子穿多少、什么时候加辅食天天闹别扭，两个人都私下跟我抱怨对方。刚才我妈又拉着我说：“你得管管你媳妇，她根本不听我的。”
reply: 妈，我知道您大老远过来帮我们带孩子，受了委屈，您跟我说我都明白。不过我不想在您和小丽之间传话，传来传去意思就变了。孩子穿多少、什么时候加辅食，这周六孩子睡午觉的时候，咱们三个坐下来一起商量个规矩，一件一件说，一个人说完另一个再说，拿不准的就一起听儿保医生的。我也会跟小丽说一样的话，不偏向谁。
note: 婆媳之间，你是孩子的爸爸，可以有自己的意见，但不当传话筒，把两个人拉到一张桌上一起定规矩。

situation: Three weeks ago I sat down with my neighbours Hal and Rosa, who'd been fighting for months over our shared driveway, and they agreed a parking schedule. It seems to be holding. I want to check in once with each of them without stirring it all up again.
reply: Hi Hal, just checking in now it's been a few weeks since we sat down about the driveway. From the outside the schedule seems to be working, and I'm really glad. If anything needs tweaking, a quick word with Rosa directly is probably the best route, and I'm happy to put the kettle on for both of you again if you'd like that. Otherwise I'll leave you to it.
note: One check-in, the same words to each of them, then genuinely step back; don't audit how the deal is going.

situation: At dinner on Saturday my best friend Sophie joked that my husband Tom 'finally found a job that sticks', and he's been fuming since. Sophie just texted asking if Tom is mad at her and whether I can smooth it over for her.
reply: Hey Soph, thanks for asking, and I'd rather Tom tell you how he took it than me guessing on his behalf. I love you both, so I'm staying out of the middle on this one. If you want to clear the air, a quick text to him directly will mean more than anything passed through me, and I'm happy to help you word it. Still on for our walk Thursday?
note: When one side is your partner, neutrality matters more: don't report his feelings, point her to him, and keep your friendship with her separate.

situation: 我和未婚夫阿哲下个月结婚。我爸妈离婚十年了，关系很僵，为了主桌怎么坐、我爸要不要带现在的妻子来，两个人都分别打电话给我，让我去跟对方说。刚才我妈又让我告诉我爸：“他要带那个人来，我就不去了。”
reply: 妈，我知道这事让您心里很不好受，您愿意跟我说，我都明白。不过我不想在您和爸之间传话，传来传去只会更僵。婚礼那天我最想要的，就是您和爸都在。座位和来宾怎么安排，我和阿哲商量好自己定，定好了分别告诉您和爸，跟他说的也会是一样的话。您有什么担心的随时跟我说，我们一起想办法让您那天待得舒服些。
note: 争的是你自己的婚礼时，不替任何一方传话，也不裁判谁对谁错，安排由你和伴侣来定，再用同样的话分别告诉两边。

situation: I'm one of three co-founders of a 9-person startup. Ana (CTO) and Ben (CEO) have been clashing for two weeks over whether to launch in November or January. Ben just DMed me: 'You were in Monday's meeting, just tell Ana she agreed to November.'
reply: Ben, I can hear how frustrated you are, and I get why the date matters so much to you. I'm not going to referee who said what on Monday or carry it to Ana; a ruling from me won't settle it between you two. What we all want is a launch that holds up. Can the three of us sit down on Friday, each of you lays out your case without interruption, and we leave with a date and what has to be true to hit it? I'll say the same to Ana.
note: Being asked to act as a witness is still being asked to pick a side; move it to a joint conversation with ground rules.
